title.narrative: Strengthening equitable access to fair justice for ALL in Samoa

description.narrative: Samoa is a small island developing state (SIDS) located in the South Pacific. The country faces a significant justice gap, where people are unable to fully benefit from equal access to justice, which hinders the country’s human development and undermines trust in public institutions.The Government of Samoa, in its current national development plan, the Pathway for the Development of Samoa (PDS FY2021/22-FY2025/26), has affirmed its commitment to upholding the rule of law and ensuring greater access to legal services and justice. This commitment is reflected in the expected outcomes of the plan under Key Priority Area 12 (KPA 12), which focuses on the protection of children, women, and the most vulnerable in society, including survivors of domestic violence. Critically, notable gaps in the sector are the lack of equal access to justice services in both criminal and civil proceedings, regardless of socio-economic status, affordability of legal services, which results in many Samoans refraining from filing a complaint or initiating a legal procedure, therefore puts the effectiveness and efficiency of the current legal aid scheme into question. Leveraging on the comparative advantages of UNDP in partnership with the Government through the Ministry of Justice Courts Administration, this Initiation Plan will employ an inclusive and a whole of society approach at the sectoral level to strengthening equitable access to fair justice through the effective delivery of the following Outputs 1) Comprehensive review and situational analysis of Samoa’s legal aid scheme and operational frameworks, and gender-based violence case management undertaken. 2) Informed by the findings of the Review and Situational Analysis, the Gender Responsive Legal Aid Policy for Samoa developed, and 3) Governance, monitoring and evaluation systems and national operators and service provides of the Legal Aid Programme and Policy are adequately enabled and capacitated.
